title: Energy & Its Forms
description: Grade 4 Science: energy and its forms — light, heat, sound, electrical and movement energy. The Sun as our energy star, how energy changes form, and saving energy.

topics.title: What Is Energy?
topics.concept:
Energy is the power to do work or to make things happen. Nothing can move, grow, glow or make sound without energy.

  • 🏃 You use energy to run and play (you get it from food).
  • 🚗 A car uses energy from fuel to move.
  • 💡 A bulb uses electrical energy to give light.

We cannot see energy itself, but we can see what it DOES.

recap: Energy is the power to do work or make things happen.
Nothing moves, grows or glows without energy.
We cannot see energy, but we see what it does.

wonder.text: You need it to run, a car needs it to move, a bulb needs it to glow. This invisible 'power to do work' is called energy.

qa.q: Where do humans get their energy?
qa.a: From the food we eat! Our body breaks down food and turns it into energy, which we use to move, grow, think and stay warm.
Not directly — energy is invisible. But we see its effects: a glowing bulb (light energy), a moving fan (motion energy), or feel a warm stove (heat energy).

topics.title: Forms of Energy
topics.concept:
Energy comes in many forms. Some common ones are:

  • 💡 Light energy — from the Sun, a bulb or a flame.
  • 🔥 Heat energy — from fire, a stove or the Sun.
  • 🔊 Sound energy — from a drum, a bell or our voice.
  • 🔌 Electrical energy — from a plug socket or a battery.
  • 🏃 Movement (motion) energy — in anything that moves, like a running child or a moving car.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 360 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="360" height="150" fill="#fffbe6"/><text x="36" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">💡</text><text x="36" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Light</text><text x="108" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🔥</text><text x="108" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Heat</text><text x="180" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🔊</text><text x="180" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Sound</text><text x="252" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🔌</text><text x="252" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Electric</text><text x="324" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🏃</text><text x="324" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Motion</text></svg>
recap: Light, heat, sound, electrical and motion are common forms.
Each form can do different kinds of work.

wonder.text: Sunlight, a warm fire, a loud drum, a moving car — these are all different forms of energy. How many can you spot at home?

qa.q: Does a battery have energy inside it?
qa.a: Yes! A battery stores chemical energy. When you put it in a toy, that stored energy turns into electrical energy and then movement, light or sound.

qa.q: Is a stretched rubber band energy?
qa.a: Yes — a stretched band or a wound-up spring stores energy. Let it go and that stored energy turns into movement. Clever!

topics.title: The Sun: Our Energy Star
topics.concept:
The Sun is the biggest and most important source of energy for our Earth. It gives us light and heat for free, every day.

  • 🌱 Plants use the Sun's light to make food — and that feeds all animals.
  • ☀️ The Sun's heat drives the water cycle, the wind and the weather.
  • 🔋 We can even catch sunlight with solar panels to make electricity.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 170" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="300" height="170" fill="#fffbe6"/><circle cx="60" cy="60" r="30" fill="#FFC93C"/><g stroke="#FFD24D" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"><line x1="60" y1="22" x2="60" y2="12"/><line x1="98" y1="60" x2="108" y2="60"/></g><defs><marker id="e2" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="4" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L9 4 L0 8 z" fill="#FFC93C"/></marker></defs><g stroke="#FFC93C" stroke-width="3" stroke-dasharray="5 4" marker-end="url(#e2)"><line x1="92" y1="78" x2="190" y2="110"/></g><text x="215" y="120" font-size="44" text-anchor="middle">🌱</text><text x="150" y="158" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#b26a00" text-anchor="middle">The Sun powers life on Earth</text></svg>
recap: The Sun is Earth's biggest source of energy.
Plants use sunlight to make food for all living things.
Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity.

wonder.text: Almost all the energy on Earth can be traced back to one place in the sky. What is it?

qa.q: How does the Sun's energy reach us in our food?
qa.a: Plants trap the Sun's light to make food. When we eat plants (or animals that ate plants), we take in that Sun energy. So the Sun feeds us all!
Solar energy is energy we get from the Sun. Solar panels soak up sunlight and turn it into electricity — a clean, free energy from our star.

topics.title: Energy Can Change Form
topics.concept:
Energy can change from one form into another — this is one of its most useful tricks!

  • 🔦 A torch: electrical energy → light energy.
  • 🔔 A bell: movement energy → sound energy.
  • 🍞 A toaster: electrical energy → heat energy.
  • 🌱 A plant: light energy → stored food energy.

Energy is never lost — it just changes from one form into another.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="300" height="150" fill="#fff"/><text x="70" y="80" font-size="44" text-anchor="middle">🔦</text><defs><marker id="e3" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="4" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L9 4 L0 8 z" fill="#FFC93C"/></marker></defs><g stroke="#FFC93C" stroke-width="4" marker-end="url(#e3)"><line x1="110" y1="70" x2="200" y2="70"/></g><text x="235" y="80" font-size="40" text-anchor="middle">💡</text><text x="150" y="130" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#b26a00" text-anchor="middle">Electrical → Light energy</text></svg>
recap: Energy can change from one form to another.
A torch: electrical → light; a bell: movement → sound.
Energy is never lost, only changed.

wonder.text: When you switch on a torch, electrical energy becomes light. Can energy really change from one form to another?

qa.q: When I rub my hands fast, why do they get warm?
qa.a: Rubbing your hands is movement energy. The rubbing changes some of that movement energy into heat energy, so your hands feel warm!
No — energy is never destroyed. It only changes form. The energy from your food becomes movement, heat and even sound when you run and laugh.

topics.title: Saving Energy
topics.concept:
Much of our electricity is made by burning fuels like coal, which can run out and cause pollution. So we must use energy wisely.

  • 💡 Switch off lights, fans and the TV when not in use.
  • ☀️ Use natural sunlight in the daytime.
  • 🚲 Walk or cycle for short trips instead of using a vehicle.
  • 🔋 Use solar, wind and water — these clean energies never run out.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="320" height="150" fill="#eafff2"/><text x="53.333333333333336" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">💡</text><text x="53.333333333333336" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Switch off</text><text x="160" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">☀️</text><text x="160" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Use daylight</text><text x="266.6666666666667" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🚲</text><text x="266.6666666666667" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Cycle</text><text x="160" y="138" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#555" text-anchor="middle">Save energy, save the planet</text></svg>
recap: Much electricity comes from burning fuels that run out and pollute.
Save energy: switch off, use daylight, walk or cycle.
Sun, wind and water are clean energies that never run out.

wonder.text: Every time we waste electricity, we waste fuel and harm our planet. How can you save energy at home?

qa.a: Much electricity comes from burning coal, which pollutes the air and will run out one day. Saving electricity saves fuel, money and keeps our air cleaner.
Renewable energy comes from sources that never run out — like the Sun, wind and flowing water. Using them is clean and good for the planet.

questions.explanation: Energy is the power to do work or make things happen.
A bulb gives out light energy (and some heat).

questions.q: Earth's biggest source of energy is…
questions.explanation: The Sun gives Earth light and heat energy every day.

questions.q: A torch changes electrical energy into…
questions.explanation: A torch turns electrical energy into light energy.
Switching off lights you are not using saves energy.

questions.q: Which is a clean energy that never runs out?
questions.explanation: Solar energy from the Sun is clean and never runs out.

questions.q: When you rub your hands quickly, movement energy changes into…
questions.explanation: Rubbing changes movement energy into heat, so your hands feel warm.

questions.q: A plant changes light energy into…
questions.explanation: A plant traps light energy and stores it as food energy.

options: Much of it comes from fuels that pollute and run out
questions.explanation: Most electricity comes from burning fuels that pollute and will run out.

questions.q: A stretched rubber band stores energy. Let it go and it becomes…
questions.explanation: The stored energy in the stretched band turns into movement when released.
Energy is never destroyed — it only changes from one form to another.
